Union Minister of Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman concludes extensive pre-budget consultations for Union Budget 2027-28
articles.full_content:
More than 200 stakeholders representing 13 sectors and stakeholder groups participated in the pre-budget consultations
Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman chaired a series of pre-budget consultation meetings for the preparation of the Union Budget 2027-28 between 16 and 26 November 2026 .
Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the 13th and final Pre-Budget Consultation with Yuva for the upcoming Union Budget 2027-28, in New Delhi, today.
More than 200 stakeholders representing 13 sectors and stakeholder groups participated in the consultations. These included industry associations, domain experts, leaders of India Inc, academics, youth representatives and practitioners from Agriculture and Rural Development; Manufacturing; MSMEs and Startups; Capital Markets and Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI); Information Technology; Infrastructure, Energy and Sustainability; Employment and Labour; Housing, Urbanisation and Culture; Health and Social Issues; Research & Development and Higher Education; School Education, Vocational Education, Skilling and Sports; Youth Affairs; and Economics. The consultation meeting with youth representatives was a novel initiative this year.
Ms. Anuradha Thakur , Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs; Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran , Chief Economic Adviser; senior officials of the Ministry of Finance; and Secretaries of Ministries and Departments concerned also participated in the discussions.
The consultations generated a wide range of forward-looking recommendations aimed at strengthening India's human capital, innovation ecosystem, manufacturing competitiveness, agricultural productivity, housing security, and educational outcomes. Stakeholders emphasized the need for reforms that can further accelerate economic growth while ensuring broad-based and inclusive development.
Among the key suggestions received were measures to promote the domestic manufacturing of biofertilisers and advanced biotechnology-based agricultural inputs; initiatives to enhance India's competitiveness in Artificial Intelligence through the development of sector-specific AI models optimised for locally available hardware; programmes to strengthen cyber-hygiene awareness among MSMEs and smaller financial institutions; and targeted interventions to support rural youth and workers in transitioning to productive non-farm employment and sustainable enterprises.
Participants also recommended launching a nationwide reading movement to ensure that every child can read and comprehend a newspaper by the end of Grade 5. In the housing sector, stakeholders highlighted the importance of promoting rental housing as a significant avenue for expanding affordable housing in urban areas. Suggestions were also made to accelerate the development of Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities to support young Indians as they transition from education to employment and to entrepreneurship.

MoSPI launches State Dashboard on eSankhyiki to improve access to State-level statistics
articles.full_content:
Effective dissemination of official statistics requires that users can readily find the data they need, access them in usable formats and reuse them for analysis. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) developed eSankhyiki as a one-stop window for official statistics. The portal enables users to search datasets, explore indicators through interactive visualisations, and consult the accompanying metadata. Users can access data through direct downloads in machine-readable formats and through Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), which allow data to be retrieved and used in other applications. Currently, the eSankhyiki portal hosts 43 statistical products with 1109 datasets comprising more than 139 million records.
The Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR) places emphasis on strengthening subnational statistics and expanding the use of digital tools across statistical processes, including dissemination. Through its Support for Statistical Strengthening component, the scheme seeks to strengthen the capacity of States and Union Territories to produce more granular statistics, including at the district level, and support their use in local planning and policymaking.
In keeping with this emphasis on subnational statistics and digital dissemination, MoSPI has launched the State Dashboard on the eSankhyiki portal. The dashboard brings together State-level data for selected indicators already available across statistical products on the portal. It has been developed in collaboration with the Institute for Competitiveness.
The dashboard currently presents 283 indicators of 21 statistical products across 10 broad themes , including agriculture, education, work and wages, and gender and inclusion. Users can select a State and a theme to view the available indicators, or explore a theme across States. Interactive charts and filters support data exploration, while the accompanying metadata and statistical notes provide the context needed to interpret the figures. Users can also download the underlying data and metadata, and download or share visualisations. By bringing together indicators from multiple statistical products into coherent, theme-based State profiles, the State Dashboard strengthens the transition from data availability to effective data utilisation.
Through this initiative, MoSPI reiterates its commitment to strengthening the country's statistical ecosystem by leveraging technology and innovation to make official statistics more accessible, transparent, interoperable and useful for informed decision-making. The dashboard will be expanded progressively and additional indicators will be added. This forms part of the ongoing effort of MoSPI to improve access to subnational statistics for policy, planning and research.
The State Dashboard will be accessible through the eSankhyiki portal at https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in
articles.summary: Effective dissemination of official statistics requires that users can readily find the data they need, access them in usable formats and reuse them for analysis. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) developed eSankhyiki as a one-stop window for official statistics. The portal enables users to search datasets, explore indicators through interactive visualisations, and consult the accompanying metadata.

PIB’s ‘Varta’ Programme Held at Khumulwng; Focus on Awareness about Drug-Free India, Census and Waste Management
articles.full_content:
Agartala, 26 November 2026: The Press Information Bureau (PIB), Agartala Branch, today organised a discussion-based ‘Varta’ programme at Khumulwng, focusing on building a drug-free India, ensuring public participation in the Census and promoting proper waste management. Speakers highlighted the important role of the media and journalists in creating awareness about these three key issues.
The programme was held at the Office of the Chief Officer, Agriculture Department, Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC). Runeil Debbarma, Chief Executive Member of TTAADC, attended as the Chief Guest. Jitendra Debbarma, Member of the District Council, and Ranjit Debbarma, Editor of ‘Chini Khorang’ and Secretary of Khumulwng Press Club, were present as Guests of Honour. Bishu Karmakar, Member-Secretary of the Tripura State Pollution Control Board, and Debashish Lodh, retired Assistant Director of the Department of Information and Cultural Affairs, participated as expert speakers.
Runeil Debbarma thanked PIB for organising the programme and stressed the need to raise awareness at every level of society for its overall progress. He said public awareness and participation are essential not only for building a drug-free society but also for proper waste management and the successful conduct of the Census.
Ranjit Debbarma highlighted the importance of the Nasha Mukt Bharat campaign and said that creating awareness is crucial to achieving its goal. He also underlined the important role of journalists in spreading awareness among people through the media.
Bishu Karmakar spoke in detail about waste management. He said improper waste management can damage drainage systems and harm the ecosystem of water bodies, directly and indirectly affecting public health. He also noted that waste is now increasingly being viewed as a resource. According to him, around 1.6 to 1.7 lakh tonnes of waste are generated in the country every day. He explained the four categories of waste that need to be segregated— wet waste, dry waste, sanitary waste and special care waste. He also discussed the new rules related to waste management. Highlighting the role of journalists in bringing cases of improper waste management to the notice of the concerned departments, he said that every urban local body in Tripura has a waste management system in place.
Debashish Lodh described the Nasha Mukt Bharat campaign as a social mass movement and said that it cannot be successful overnight. Everyone must come forward to build a drug-free society, and journalists have a responsibility to raise public awareness in this regard. He observed that everyone is a soldier in the mission to build a drug-free India.
Speaking on the Census, Debashish Lodh said that the country's development plans and future policies depend on accurate Census data. People's participation is essential for comprehensive planning. However, many people either provide incorrect information or withhold details during the Ce
articles.summary: Agartala, 26 November 2026: The Press Information Bureau (PIB), Agartala Branch, today organised a discussion-based ‘Varta’ programme at Khumulwng, focusing on building a drug-free India, ensuring public participation in the Census and promoting proper waste management. Speakers highlighted the important role of the media and journalists in creating awareness about these three key issues. The programme was held at the Office of the Chief Officer, Agriculture Department, Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC).

MSDE partners with Ministry of Jal Shakti to skill one lakh youth under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
articles.full_content:
The initiative will leverage the nationwide network of ITIs and NSTIs to develop a skilled workforce for rural water supply operations and maintenance
In an effort to align vocational training with emerging employment opportunities in the rural water sector, the Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti. The partnership will focus on implementing the Water Supply Operation & Maintenance Skilling Programme (Nal Jal Mitra) under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.
The initiative aims to train and certify at least one lakh candidates, with an estimated financial outlay of ₹111.93 crore, entirely funded by DDWS.
The MoU was signed in the presence of Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; Shri C. R. Patil, Union Minister of Jal Shakti; and Shri V. Somanna, Minister of State, Jal Shakti.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, underscored that the initiative represents a significant example of inter-ministerial convergence aimed at addressing the skilled manpower requirements of a key national programme. He highlighted that the country's extensive network of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) offers an effective platform for imparting specialised skills required for rural water supply operations and maintenance.
The 165-hour training programme has been developed by the Central Staff Training and Research Institute (CSTARI) under DGT, in consultation with DDWS. It will be offered as an optional elective to existing and former trainees of the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) Fitter and Plumber trades across ITIs and NSTIs.
The programme combines 120 hours of institutional training with 45 hours of mandatory on-the-job training. Candidates will learn plumbing, water distribution, pump and motor maintenance, basic electrical work and water quality monitoring. Upon successful completion, trainees will receive a National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF)-aligned short-term training certificate from DGT in addition to their National Trade Certificate (NTC).
The National Instructional Media Institute (NIMI), under DGT, will oversee training coordination, assessment, certification and fund disbursement. DDWS will make the details of certified candidates available at the district and Gram Panchayat levels, where they may be engaged for work as per the policies of the respective states.
Nearly 16 crore rural households in India now have tap water connections. Keeping these water supply systems functional requires trained personnel at the village level. The programme seeks to meet this requirement and, in the process, open up employment avenues for rural youth.

The partnership will focus on implementing the Water Supply Operation & Maintenance Skilling Programme (Nal Jal Mitra) under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. The initiative aims to train and certify at least one lakh candidates, with an estimated financial outlay of ₹111.93 crore, entirely funded by DDWS.

articles.full_content:
Ministry of Jal Shakti partners with Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship to strengthen the skilled workforce for sustainable rural water supply services Initiative to Create New Employment Opportunities for Rural Youth by Building a Skilled Local Workforce of ‘Nal Jal Mitras’ Programme to Roll Out Water Supply Operation and Maintenance Training Through ITIs and NSTIs Nationwide
In a significant stride towards ensuring long-term sustainability of rural drinking water infrastructure and generating local employment, the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS) , Ministry of Jal Shakti (MoJS), and the Directorate General of Training (DGT) , Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the Water Supply Operation & Maintenance Skilling Programme (Nal Jal Mitra) under the Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 (JJM 2.0) .
The MoU was signed in the presence of Shri C. R. Patil, Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri V. Somanna, Hon’ble Minister of State, Jal Shakti and Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Hon’ble Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, at the residence office of Hon’ble MoJS, New Delhi.
The agreement was formally executed by Smt. Swati Meena Naik, Joint Secretary, NJJM and Shri Sunil Kumar Gupta , Deputy Director General, DGT. Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MoSDE, Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, NJJM, and senior officials from both Ministries were present during the MoU signing.
The Hon’ble Union Ministers present on the occasion appreciated the initiative, highlighting its significance in strengthening rural water supply systems through a skilled local workforce and creating livelihood opportunities for rural youth. They acknowledged the importance of inter-ministerial collaboration under the ‘whole of government’ approach in leveraging the country’s vocational training infrastructure to support the objectives of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.
Briefing on Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 and the skilling initiative, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena , Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, said that with nearly 16 crore rural households now connected through tap water supply systems, the next priority is establishing a robust operation and maintenance ecosystem capable of supporting these assets over the long term. He stressed that timely technical support should be available within villages and nearby areas so that routine operational issues can be addressed quickly without dependence on external agencies.
Shri Meena highlighted that the partnership between DDWS and DGT would connect India's vocational training ecosystem directly with the rural water sector. Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and Data Security Council of India (DSCI) sign MoU to enable trusted data sharing for official statistics
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and the Data Security Council of India (DSCI), set up by Nasscom, a not-for-profit industry body and think tank on data protection and cyber security, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in New Delhi today. Dr Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI, Shri Vinayak Godse, Chief Executive Officer, DSCI, and senior officers of the Ministry were present on the occasion. The MoU forms part of the Ministry’s efforts to strengthen the National Statistical System through collaboration with public and private sector institutions.
Statistical agencies now-a-days use data from both traditional and alternative sources, some of which contain personal identifiers. With Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 scheduled to come into force in 2027, data producing agencies need to gear up themselves by reviewing how they handle such data while maintaining privacy and confidentiality. This partnership will help develop protocols for sharing data in trusted manner within and across agencies while maintaining data quality, protecting privacy and preserving statistical confidentiality. As a first step, MoSPI and DSCI will jointly prepare a policy paper on trusted data flows and data management, drawing on international good practices in data protection and cybersecurity.
The collaboration will also cover joint research on data governance and technical support for the adoption of privacy-enhancing technologies and the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI). The MoU also provides facilitation for pilot projects with industry, academia, research institutions and international organisations and it will strengthen the national statistical ecosystem, by enabling responsible adoption of AI and emerging technologies.

PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry Records ₹4,385.28 Crore Incentive Disbursement in FY 2026–27
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) continues to strengthen India's automobile and auto component manufacturing ecosystem through the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry. The scheme aims to enhance domestic manufacturing capabilities, promote advanced automotive technologies and position India as a global hub for automobile manufacturing.
Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel, Shri H. D. Kumaraswamy, chaired a review meeting with Dr. Hanif Qureshi, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), today to review the progress and implementation of the PLI-Auto Scheme.
Accelerated Incentive Disbursement under the PLI-Auto Scheme
With a total approved budgetary outlay of ₹25,938 crore, the PLI-Auto Scheme has made significant progress in promoting investments, strengthening domestic supply chains and encouraging the manufacturing of Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products. During FY 2026–27, incentive disbursements under the scheme reached ₹4,385.28 crore as of 25 th November 2026. The cumulative incentive disbursement under the scheme since its inception has reached ₹6,771.64 crore.
Strong Investment, Incremental Sales and Employment Generation
The scheme has also recorded encouraging progress in attracting investments and generating employment. As of 30 th September 2026, approved applicants had reported cumulative investments of ₹52,806 crore, surpassing the targeted investment of ₹42,500 crore. The scheme has also facilitated incremental sales of ₹82,993 crore over the base year FY 2019–20 and generated 77,755 employment opportunities, reflecting its contribution to strengthening India's automotive manufacturing ecosystem.
Strengthening Domestic Manufacturing and Value Addition
Promoting domestic value addition remains a key objective of the PLI-Auto Scheme. The scheme mandates a minimum Domestic Value Addition (DVA) of 50% for eligible products to qualify for incentives. As of 25 th November 2026, DVA certificates have been issued to 9 Champion OEMs covering 139 products/variants, and 10 Component Champions covering 53 products/variants. This progress reflects the growing domestic capabilities in manufacturing advanced automotive products and components.
The initiative is aligned with the Government of India's vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat, reinforcing the country's commitment to becoming a leading global destination for automobile and auto component manufacturing. The Ministry of Heavy Industries remains committed to supporting the growth of a robust, resilient and technologically advanced automotive industry through sustained policy initiatives and industry collaboration.

Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas to visit PDEU; to see National Core Repository and interact with students on Energy Transition
articles.full_content:
Senior officers of ONGC and IOCL to accompany the Hon'ble Minister
HHon'ble Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, will visit Pandit Deendayal Energy University (PDEU), Gandhinagar, on Friday (27th November).. The Hon'ble Minister is scheduled to arrive on campus at 2:30 p.m. and will be accompanied by senior officers of Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) and Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL). During the visit, the Hon'ble Minister will tour the National Core Repository and will thereafter interact with a select group of PDEU students on the theme of Energy Transition.
National Core Repository
The National Core Repository (NCR) at Gandhinagar was established under the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH), Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, as a national facility for the preservation, curation and scientific study of drill cores recovered from India's sedimentary basins. Cores held at national repositories are treated as a national asset, with access governed by DGH, and constitute a primary scientific record of the country's subsurface. The facility supports basin studies, reservoir characterisation and exploration research by academia, national oil companies and industry.
PDEU will be housing about 1 lakh metre cores from onshore and offshore basins of India. To start with the university is focusing on 5 basins.
Interaction with students on Energy Transition
The Hon'ble Minister will address and take questions from students drawn from across the University's schools of petroleum technology, energy technology, management and liberal studies. The session is intended as an open exchange on India's energy transition pathway, the role of natural gas as a transition fuel, green hydrogen, biofuels and ethanol blending, carbon capture, and the skills and research capacity the sector will require of the next generation of energy professionals.
PDEU and the energy transition
The University was reconstituted from Pandit Deendayal Petroleum University to Pandit Deendayal Energy University in 2020, reflecting a deliberate widening of its mandate from hydrocarbons to the full energy spectrum. Research at the University today spans solar, wind, hydrogen, geothermal, bioenergy and energy storage, aligned to India's net-zero commitment.
Among the University's dedicated facilities are the Centre of Excellence for Geothermal Energy (CEGE), established in 2013 with the support of the Government of Gujarat; the Solar Research and Development Centre; the Centre for Biofuel and Bioenergy Studies; the International Automobile Centre of Excellence; and the SIEMENS Centre of Excellence. The Department of Science and Technology sanctioned a Technology Enabling Centre at PDEU in 2023 on the theme of Energy, Health and Water, to carry laboratory research through prototype, validation and field trial to industry adoption.

DPIIT Concludes Special Campaign 6 with Significant Achievements in Swachhata and Reduction of Pendency
articles.full_content:
Biomass Gasifier Installed at NCCBM’s Ballabgarh Campus to Promote Sustainable Waste-to-Energy Conversion DPIIT Achieves 100% Disposal of Public Grievances Under Special Campaign 6, Reclaims 18,644 Sq. Ft. of Office Space
The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), along with its attached and subordinate offices, concluded Special Campaign 6 under the guidance of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The campaign, aimed at institutionalising the principles of Swachhata (cleanliness) and minimising pendency in official work, was undertaken across all offices to promote cleanliness, efficiency and effective record management.
Special Campaign 6 was conducted from 2nd of October to 31st of October 2026, preceded by a preparatory phase from 15th of September to 30th September 2026. Throughout the campaign, DPIIT undertook focused efforts to promote awareness about cleanliness, systematic record management and the timely disposal of pending cases. With near-total achievement of the identified targets and notable progress across various campaign parameters, DPIIT reaffirmed its commitment to institutionalising Swachhata, fostering a culture of efficiency and responsiveness, and strengthening sustainable practices in government functioning.
As part of the campaign, the National Council for Cement and Building Materials (NCCBM), an autonomous organisation under DPIIT, installed a biomass gasifier at its Ballabgarh campus in Haryana. The gasifier uses biomass, wood and refuse-derived fuel (RDF) as feedstock to produce a combustible gas known as Syngas. During the campaign, NCCBM successfully conducted a trial run using 150 kg of dry horticultural waste. The waste was first shredded and subsequently converted into Syngas through partial oxidation at elevated temperatures under a controlled supply of gasifying agents. The potential utilisation of the Syngas generated through this process in power generation and diesel generator (DG) sets will be explored further. Trial runs using Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) obtained from Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) were also conducted in the gasifier during the campaign. This initiative showcases an environmentally sustainable approach to waste-to-energy conversion and offers a replicable model for promoting sustainable infrastructure, resource recovery and the principles of a circular economy.
In addition to this initiative, DPIIT made significant progress across other key parameters of the campaign. Its attached and subordinate offices undertook the disposal of scrap materials and e-waste, resulting in the reclamation of 18,644 square feet of office space and the generation of ₹16,52,569 in revenue. The Department also achieved 100% completion in the disposal of public grievances and nearly 100% completion across other key parameters, including public grievance appeals, review of e-files and physical files, and cleanliness activities.
